newsitem.title: FRANCE: MEPs back 50 pct risk weighting for certain loans.
newsitem.headline: MEPs back 50 pct risk weighting for certain loans.

text.p: A draft directive which would allow mortgage-backed securities to be given the same risk weightings as mortgage loans won approval from the European Parliament on Tuesday.
MEPs backed a European Commission proposal - COM(95)709 - which amends a 1989 directive setting a solvency ratio for credit institutions.
The amendment means that mortgage-backed loans for offices and multi-purpose commercial premises can be given a risk weighting of 50 percent until January 1, 2001.
In the case of normal risks, credit institutions are obliged to reserve own capital amounting to eight percent of the volume of credit granted. This corresponds to a risk weighting of 100 percent.
When the credit is granted to a bank or state structure and the risk is particularly low, the weighting is set at between zero and 20 percent.
This enables the credit institution to reduce its own capital reserve to 1.6 or even zero percent of the volume of credit granted.

According to rapporteur Marlies Mosiek-Urbahn, a German Christian Democrat, surveys have shown that the rates of default on long-term financing for offices and multi-purpose commercial premises can be as low as for housing credit, which attracts a risk weighting of 50 percent.
Parliament agreed with the Commission that the member states' banking regulatory authorities should therefore be allowed to weight this type of credit at 50 percent too.
The change would have the added advantage of establishing equal treatment with commercial property leasing which, under the solvency directive, is also to be weighted at 50 percent.
